title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: First published serially between 1879 and 1880, The Brothers Karamazov centres on the murder of Fyodor Pavlovitch Karamazov and the lives of his sons Dmitri, Ivan and Alyosha.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition adds extensive original material on Dostoevsky, Russian law and religion, the novel’s real-life sources, money and social rank, the Grand Inquisitor, publication history and critical reception.
editionIncludes: Historical context, themes and character studies
Critical perspectives, glossary and original context essays

title: Carmilla
author: Sheridan Le Fanu
summary: First serialised in The Dark Blue from December 1871 to March 1872, Carmilla follows Laura’s encounter with the beautiful and increasingly disturbing guest who arrives at her isolated Styrian home.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition adds original material on Le Fanu, eighteenth-century vampire reports, the story’s literary sources, its original magazine publication and its long afterlife.
editionIncludes: The complete 1872 text with the Hesselius Prologue
Historical context on vampires, Styria and the Habsburg world
Critical perspectives, glossary and publication history

title: Common Sense and The American Crisis
author: Thomas Paine
image: Common sense and The American Tragedy Main Cover.png
summary: Common Sense first appeared anonymously in Philadelphia on 10 January 1776. This edition follows the enlarged Bradford text dated 14 February, including the Appendix and Address to the People called Quakers.
descriptionParagraphs: The American Crisis follows the war from the retreat of 1776 through independence and peace, comprising thirteen numbered papers, the Crisis Extraordinary and two Supernumerary papers. The edition adds original material on Paine, printing and piracy, political and military context, contemporary rebuttals and later reception.
editionIncludes: The complete enlarged 1776 text of Common Sense
All 16 pieces of The American Crisis
Historical context, critical perspectives and glossary

title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
author: Leo Tolstoy
image: Death of Ivan Ilych Main Cover.png
summary: First published in 1886, The Death of Ivan Ilyich follows a successful Russian official whose apparently ordinary life is overturned by illness and the knowledge of his approaching death.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition adds original material on Tolstoy, the judicial reforms of 1864, nineteenth-century medicine, the chronology of Ivan Ilyich’s career, language, publication and critical reception.
editionIncludes: The complete Louise and Aylmer Maude translation
Historical context on Russian law, medicine and social rank
Character studies, reception history and glossary

title: E. F. Benson Ghost Stories
author: E. F. Benson
image: E.F Benson Ghost Stories Main Cover.png
summary: Combining The Room in the Tower and Other Stories (1912) and Visible and Invisible (1923), this volume brings together two of E. F. Benson’s major supernatural collections in full. The two books contain seventeen and twelve stories respectively.
descriptionParagraphs: Stories included: The Room in the Tower; The Dust-Cloud; Gavon’s Eve; The Confession of Charles Linkworth; At Abdul Ali’s Grave; The Shootings of Achnaleish; How Fear Departed from the Long Gallery; Caterpillars; The Cat; The Bus-Conductor; The Man Who Went Too Far; Between the Lights; Outside the Door; The Terror by Night; The Other Bed; The Thing in the Hall; The House with the Brick-Kiln; And the Dead Spake——; The Outcast; The Horror-Horn; Machaon; Negotium Perambulans; At the Farmhouse; Inscrutable Decrees; The Gardener; Mr. Tilly’s Séance; Mrs. Amworth; In the Tube; and Roderick’s Story.

title: Heart of Darkness
author: Joseph Conrad
summary: First published in three instalments in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine from February to April 1899, Heart of Darkness appeared in book form in Youth: A Narrative, and Two Other Stories on 13 November 1902.
descriptionParagraphs: Marlow’s journey upriver in search of the ivory agent Kurtz draws heavily on Conrad’s own experience in the Congo Free State in 1890, while transforming the historical record into one of the most debated works of modern English fiction.
This edition adds original material on Conrad’s life and sources, the Congo Free State, narrative structure, language, major critical debates, reception history and the surviving documentary record.
editionIncludes: Historical context on the Congo Free State
Critical perspectives and a documentary record

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
image: Hound of the Baskervilles Main Cover.png
summary: When Sir Charles Baskerville dies on the edge of Dartmoor, the evidence points towards an old family legend: a monstrous hound said to pursue the Baskerville line. Sherlock Holmes is sceptical, but the arrival of Sir Henry Baskerville brings new threats and sends Dr Watson to the moor in search of an explanation.
descriptionParagraphs: First serialised in The Strand Magazine from August 1901 to April 1902, The Hound of the Baskervilles appeared in book form on 25 March 1902. The first edition contained sixteen of Sidney Paget’s sixty illustrations for the serial.

title: White Nights
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: First published in 1848 and revised by Dostoevsky in 1860, White Nights follows an isolated young dreamer through four meetings with Nastenka during St Petersburg’s luminous summer nights.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition adds original material on the city, the phenomenon of the white nights, Dostoevsky’s literary sources, the story’s language, characters, publication and afterlife.
editionIncludes: Character studies, critical material and glossary

title: The Rape of the Lock and An Essay on Criticism
author: Alexander Pope
image: The rape of the lock and essay on criticism main cover.png
summary: The Rape of the Lock turns the cutting of Arabella Fermor’s hair into an elaborate mock-epic of sylphs, fashionable society, ombre and heroic combat. An Essay on Criticism sets out Pope’s arguments about nature, taste, learning, poetic technique and the proper conduct of the critic.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition presents the poems in their later forms and adds original material on Pope’s life, sources and influences, eighteenth-century society, the game of ombre, the reading public, reception history and the critical debates surrounding both works. The manuscript’s editorial apparatus is extensive, running from historical context and character studies through critical perspectives, glossary and teaching pathways.
editionIncludes: Explanatory footnotes keyed to the text
Historical context, critical perspectives and glossary

title: The Overcoat
author: Nikolai Gogol
summary: First published in Gogol’s collected Works in 1842, The Overcoat follows the obscure clerk Akaki Akakievitch from his copying desk to the purchase, loss and strange afterlife of a new greatcoat.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition adds original material on St Petersburg, the Table of Ranks, money and clothing, Gogol’s narrative style, the story’s sources, reception, translations and adaptations.
editionIncludes: Five Story So Far and Context sections
Historical context, critical perspectives, glossary and teaching pathways

title: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
author: William Blake
image: Somgs of Innocence and Experience Main Cover.png
summary: First issued separately as Songs of Innocence in 1789 and Songs of Experience in 1794, Blake later brought the two together under the subtitle Shewing the Two Contrary States of the Human Soul. The surviving copies vary in arrangement, colouring and detail because Blake printed and finished them by hand.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition places the poems alongside reproductions of Blake’s relief-etched designs and adds original material on illuminated printing, the movement of poems between the two collections, Blake’s sources, historical context, paired poems, critical perspectives and reception. The manuscript also includes a glossary, bibliography and teaching pathways
editionIncludes: The complete collection with line numbering
Historical context, critical perspectives and glossary

title: Notes from Underground
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: First published in 1864, Notes from Underground combines a furious attack on rational utopianism with the confession of an isolated, self-defeating narrator.
descriptionParagraphs: This edition adds original material on Chernyshevsky and rational egoism, the Crystal Palace, Russian society in the 1860s, Dostoevsky’s censored passage, language, reception and later influence.
editionIncludes: Critical perspectives, glossary and publication history
